gen.title: Gene pool fitness and related definitions

cards.stem: What is a gene pool described as in the material
options: unique set of alleles
complete fossil record
identical twin pair
single parental lineage
cards.quote: A gene pool is the unique set of alleles that could be found by analyzing the DNA from every member of a species or population.
cards.hint: Recall the definition that lists all alleles in a group

cards.stem: How is fitness defined for an organism in a population
options: probability of transmitting one's genes to the next generation
count of visible traits per individual
total number of cell divisions
rate of random environmental change
cards.quote: Fitness is the probability of transmitting one's genes to the next generation in relation to the average probability for that population.
cards.hint: Think about passing genes on compared to others

cards.stem: When is an individual considered heterozygous at a locus
options: two different alleles at a specific locus
two identical copies at a specific locus
absence of any allele at a locus
presence of an extra chromosome
cards.quote: If an individual has two different alleles at a specific locus, the individual is heterozygous at that locus
cards.hint: Focus on having two distinct alleles at one location

cards.stem: What tool is described as a grid for showing expected genotypes
options: grid that graphically represents expected genotypes
chart that permanently alters allele counts
table that eliminates variation within groups
diagram that measures extinction probability
cards.quote: A Punnett square is simply a grid that graphically represents expected genotypes.
cards.hint: Remember the visual grid used for genotype predictions
